problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives may be nonconvex; a global minimizer exists. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Globally, 2μ(f(x)−f*) ≤ ‖∇f(x)‖², with 0 < μ ≤ L and f(x0)−f* ≤ Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call returns g(x,ξ) using a fresh IID seed, with E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). Only gradient samples are supplied; no function values or Hessian oracle are available. All Params, including L, μ, ρ, σ, p, Δ, ε and x0, are public; f and the oracle distribution are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedPLHessian.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform central moment bound E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖^p ≤ σ^p, where 1 < p ≤ 2 and σ ≥ 0. Finite variance is not required when p < 2.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: An arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure; no dimension bound is specified.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable and its derivative satisfies ‖D∇f(x)−D∇f(y)‖op ≤ ρ‖x−y‖ globally, with ρ ≥ 0. This is Lipschitz continuity of the objective Hessian, with no samplewise smoothness requirement.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable point-valued output X with integrable objective gap and E[f(X)−f*] ≤ ε, where ε > 0. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over algorithm randomness and the IID oracle seeds. The supplied budget caps the total number of individual gradient calls deterministically, including batching and initialization.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines nonconvex global PL geometry, a globally Lipschitz Hessian, and an unbiased gradient oracle with only a bounded p-th central moment, allowing infinite variance. This is a specialized variant of standard smooth stochastic PL optimization.

descriptionHtml:
Heavy-Tailed Polyak–Łojasiewicz Minimization

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The objective has Lipschitz gradient and Hessian, satisfies a Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality, and admits a global minimizer x⋆. A given starting point x0∈E has bounded objective gap. The oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient at each query, using independent, identically distributed samples with bounded noise moments of order p∈(1,2], allowing heavy tails. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where expectation includes sampling and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ∥⋅∥ for the norm induced by the inner product and ∥⋅∥op for the induced operator norm. Fix parameters 0<μ≤L,ρ,σ,Δ≥0,1<p≤2,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, L, μ, ρ, σ, p, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Gradient and Hessian regularity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and its gradient is Fréchet differentiable. The Hessian ∇2f(x) is a linear operator from E to E. For all x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality and initialization). There exists x⋆∈E such that, for every x∈E, f(x⋆)≤f(x),2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2, and the given starting point satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased oracle with heavy-tailed noise). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For each x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥p is integrable under ν, with Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥p]≤σp. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν under their joint probability law on ΩN. At the kth query x∈E, the oracle returns g(x,ξk). Algorithm randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and have integrable objective gap, with EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the samples and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Finite-dimensional real inner-product space; f has an L-Lipschitz, differentiable gradient and ρ-Lipschitz Hessian, an attained minimum f⋆, and 2μ(f−f⋆)≤∥∇f∥2, where 0<μ≤L. Initially f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ. IID samples feed a jointly measurable unbiased gradient oracle with integrable centered pth moment at most σp, 1<p≤2; ρ,σ,Δ≥0. Target: ∫(f(xout)−f⋆)dPout≤ε, ε>0, where Pout includes the IID samples and independent uniform final-window selection.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Uniform
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedPLHessian

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 1 < p.p ∧ p.p ≤ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ∃ (g : p.E → p.Ω → p.E) (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      (∀ x, 2 * p.μ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2) ∧ f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σ ^ p.p)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedPLHessian
